definition: Visual Instruction Generation and Correction, a framework that enables multimodal large language models to generate instruction-tuning data and progressively enhance its quality on-the-fly.
details: Visual Instruction Generation and Correction, a framework that enables multimodal large language models to generate instruction-tuning data and progressively enhance its quality on-the-fly.

explainer.lead: VIGC is Visual Instruction Generation and Correction, a framework that enables multimodal large language models to generate instruction-tuning data and progressively enhance its quality on the fly. It matters because instruction-tuning data is costly to produce by hand.

tiers.eli5: It's like a student who writes their own practice questions and corrects them as they go, instead of waiting for a teacher to supply them.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to bootstrap instruction-tuning data from a multimodal model itself, with a correction step improving quality during generation. A common pitfall is that errors in the model's own generation can propagate into the tuning data.
tiers.paperLevel: A framework in which a multimodal large language model generates instruction-tuning data and progressively enhances its quality on the fly; quality is bounded by the generating model's own capabilities.

explainer.example: A multimodal model drafts image-instruction pairs and then revises weak ones before they enter the tuning set.
